To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a neural model for visual storytelling can generate coherent and meaningful stories; 2) our model is able to generate stories that are more coherent than those generated by a baseline model; 3) a model for generating stories from image sequences can be trained on image captions and vice versa.
our model showed competitive results on the Visual Storyteller Challenge 2018 in terms of METEOR metric, and human ratings.

we propose a model that uses an encoder LSTM to learn a context vector from a sequence of images and then uses multiple decoder LSTMs to generate a short story from each of the images, and our model showed competitive results in the internal track in the Visual Storytells Challenge 2018.

the problem of automatically generating short stories based on images.

the development of a neural model that generates short visual stories from an image sequence.

the model is able to tell a story by showing and telling the images.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the encoder LSTM is able to capture the story structure from the image sequence, and the decoder LSTM is able to generate a coherent and fluent story from the context vector and the image embeddings.
the context vector is a key ingredient for generating coherent and fluent stories.
a model that is trained to generate a story from a single image can be used to generate stories from an image sequence by using a context vector that is computed from the sequence.
